Diag.Title: Diagnostics
Diag.HowText: zaprett opens the check addresses of the enabled services from this PC, compares the DNS answers with encrypted DNS and tells what exactly the provider does: substitutes DNS, blocks addresses, breaks encrypted connections or slows them down.
Diag.NotYet: The check has not been made yet.
Diag.NothingToCheck: There was nothing to check: no enabled service has check addresses.
Diag.Conclusion.Some: Conclusion: {0} of {1} sites open; for the others — {2}.
Diag.NoteRunning: Checked: {0}. The bypass was running during the check, so the result shows what this PC sees with zaprett.
Diag.NoteStopped: Checked: {0}. The bypass was not running during the check, so the result shows the blocking of the provider as it is.
Diag.ConflictsText: Other programs that intercept traffic (GoodbyeDPI, another zapret, AdGuard, some VPN and network utilities) can stop the bypass or break the internet together with it.
Diag.CheckText: Builds the engine arguments from the current settings and asks the engine whether it accepts them, without restarting anything.
Diag.CheckOk: The engine accepts the current configuration.
Diag.CheckFail: The configuration does not pass the check: {0}
Diag.ReportText: Versions, state, conflicts, the last check and the log — to send to support. Addresses of subscriptions lose their parameters, so no tokens get into the report.
Diag.CopiedText: The report is in the clipboard.

Lists.Title: Lists
Lists.Lead: Which sites and networks go through the bypass. The lists of services are switched by "Services"; here you can fine-tune them, add your own sites and exclusions, and subscribe to external lists.
Lists.Mode.Whitelist: Only sites from the enabled lists (recommended)
Lists.Mode.WhitelistText: Everything else goes as usual, so banks, games and other programs are not affected.
Lists.Mode.BlacklistText: Helps with sites that are not in any list, but more sites may break; add them to the exclusions.
Lists.Domains.Text: Lists of site names. A site is processed if its name or a parent domain is in an enabled list.
Lists.Networks.Text: Lists of IP networks: for apps that connect by address without a site name (Telegram, voice chats, games).
Lists.Exclusions.Text: Sites and networks that are never processed: government services, banks, local networks. They are always on in the whitelist mode as well.
Lists.User.HintDomains: One domain per line, for example example.org (subdomains are included). Lines starting with # are comments.
Lists.User.HintIp: One address or network per line, for example 203.0.113.0/24 or 2001:db8::/32. Lines starting with # are comments.
Lists.User.ImportedText: The lines of the file are added at the end. Check them and press "Save".
Lists.Sources.Text: External lists that zaprett downloads and updates by itself. Large registries of blocked sites help with many sites at once, but many of them are blocked by address, where zaprett cannot help.
Lists.Source.IsIpset: The list contains IP networks, not site names
Lists.Source.BadUrlText: The address of a subscription must start with https://.
Lists.Source.DeleteText: The subscription "{0}" and its downloaded list will be removed.

Monitor.RepairingText: zaprett is looking for a working strategy automatically (quick selection).

Services.Title: Services
Services.Lead: Mark the services that your provider slows down or blocks. zaprett turns on ready-made lists of their sites and the always-needed exclusions (government services, banks). Services marked "Will not help" are blocked in a way that zaprett cannot bypass.
Services.AppliedText: zaprett works with the new lists.
Services.NothingSelectedText: Mark at least one service, or turn the bypass off on the home page.
Services.Err.Load: Could not load the list of services
Settings.Title: Settings
Settings.Autostart: Turn the bypass on when Windows starts
Settings.AutostartText: The zaprett service always starts with Windows; this switch decides whether the bypass is on after a restart.
Settings.EngineText: zapret (winws) suits most providers. zapret2 (winws2) has its own set of built-in strategies.
Settings.WatchdogText: Restarts the engine if it stops unexpectedly.
Settings.Ipv6Text: Turn on if your provider gives IPv6 and sites open over it without the bypass.
Settings.Dns.StateOn: On: the provider can neither see nor substitute DNS requests of this PC.
Settings.Dns.StateOff: Off: some providers substitute DNS answers for blocked sites; then the site does not open even through zaprett.
Settings.QuicText: Browsers then use ordinary HTTPS, where the bypass works. Helps when YouTube works in one browser but not in another.
Settings.GameText: An extra rule for game servers from the enabled IP network lists. Turn on only if a game from the lists does not connect.
Settings.BadPortsText: Use ports 1–65535 and ranges separated by commas, for example 1024-65535 or 80,443,50000-50100.
Settings.NetText: The bypass can work everywhere or only in chosen Wi-Fi networks, for example only at home.
Settings.Ssids: Wi-Fi network names, one per line
Settings.Corporate: Do not work in a corporate network
Settings.CorporateText: In a domain (office) network the bypass switches off by itself, so it does not interfere with work systems.
Settings.MonitorText: zaprett checks the sites of the enabled services and warns when they stop opening.
Settings.IntervalText: Each check opens a few addresses; it does not load the connection.
Settings.ThresholdText: A check fails when less than half of the sites opened.
Settings.AutoRepairText: When sites stop opening, run a quick strategy selection and switch to a better strategy (not more often than every 6 hours).
Settings.ChannelText: Beta gets new features earlier and may contain errors.
Settings.Update.InstallText: zaprett downloads the update, checks its signature and installs it. The bypass stops for a few seconds.
Settings.Update.Installing: The update is being installed; the interface restarts by itself.
Settings.LanguageText: Russian, English or Chinese. The service and the command line use the same language.
Settings.ThemeText: Light, dark or as in Windows.
Settings.NotificationsText: When sites stop opening or the strategy is replaced automatically.
Settings.CloseToTray: Keep in the notification area when closed
Settings.CloseToTrayText: The service works regardless of the interface; the icon shows the state of the bypass.
Settings.WizardText: Choose the services again from the beginning.
Settings.SavedReloaded: The changes are applied; the engine was restarted.
Shell.Down.Title: The zaprett service is not running
Shell.Down.Text: The interface works together with the zaprett Windows service, which does the bypass. The service does not answer now.

Shell.Down.StillDown: The service still does not answer. If it keeps stopping, reinstall zaprett.
Strategies.Title: Strategies
Strategies.Lead: A strategy is a set of tricks that hides the site name from the equipment of the provider. Different providers need different strategies: automatic selection finds the one that opens more sites.
Strategies.NewComment: own strategy: one profile per line, profiles separated by --new
Strategies.NewInfo: Own strategy. Its name must start with "user-".

Strategies.PickHint: Choose a strategy on the left to view it, or create your own.

Test.Lead: zaprett tries strategies one by one on the check addresses of the enabled services and keeps the one that opens more sites. The bypass for this PC keeps working meanwhile: candidates are tried by a separate test engine.
Test.QuickText: about 12 proven strategies, a few minutes
Test.FullText: all installed strategies, may take 10–20 minutes
Test.ApplyIfBetter: Apply the best one if it is better than the current
Test.ExclusiveText: As in older versions: the bypass is off during the check. Only if the usual selection does not work.
Test.ConfirmQuick: About 12 strategies will be checked; it takes a few minutes. The bypass keeps working meanwhile. Start?
Test.ConfirmFull: All installed strategies will be checked; it may take 10–20 minutes. The bypass keeps working meanwhile. Start?
Test.ConfirmExclusive: The bypass will be stopped for the whole check.
Test.Mode.Isolated: The selection runs without stopping the bypass: candidates are checked by a separate test engine.

Verdict.ok.Label: Opens
Verdict.ok.Advice: The sites open: no blocking is visible.
Verdict.dns_spoof.Label: DNS substitution
Verdict.dns_spoof.Advice: The provider substitutes DNS answers: instead of the real address of the site this PC gets the address of a stub. Changing packets does not help while the requests go to the DNS of the provider. Turn on encrypted DNS: then the provider can neither see nor substitute the requests.
Verdict.ip_block.Label: Blocked by IP address
Verdict.ip_block.Advice: The provider does not let connections to the addresses of the site through. zaprett changes only the first packets of a connection and cannot open a blocked address: such sites need a VPN or a proxy.
Verdict.tls_block.Label: Blocked by site name (TLS)
Verdict.tls_block.Advice: The connection is established, but the provider breaks it when it sees the site name at the start of the encrypted connection. This is exactly what zaprett bypasses: run automatic strategy selection.
Verdict.throttle.Label: Slowed down
Verdict.throttle.Advice: Data starts to come, but stops or freezes at about 14–24 KB: this is how the provider slows the site down. zaprett bypasses this: run automatic strategy selection.
Verdict.http_block.Label: Stub page of the provider
Verdict.http_block.Advice: Instead of the site the provider returns its own page about the blocking. Usually the provider recognises the site name in the request, which zaprett can hide: run automatic strategy selection. If it does not help, turn on encrypted DNS.
Verdict.unknown.Label: Could not be determined
Verdict.unknown.Advice: The site did not open, but it could not be determined how it is blocked. The site may be down by itself. Try automatic strategy selection; if it does not help, check the site through a VPN.
Verdict.Other.Advice: The service returned a verdict this interface does not know yet. Update zaprett.
Warn.Unknown.Title: Warning: {0}
Warn.Unknown.Text: The service reported a problem. See "Diagnostics" for details.
Warn.no_active_lists.Title: No site lists are enabled
Warn.no_active_lists.Text: In the whitelist mode zaprett bypasses blocking only for sites from the enabled lists. No list is enabled now, so the bypass affects nothing. Choose services on the "Services" page.
Warn.engine_missing.Title: The bypass engine is not installed
Warn.engine_missing.Text: The engine program (winws or winws2) was not found. Reinstall zaprett; if it disappears again, the antivirus may be removing it.
Warn.no_strategy.Title: No strategy is selected
Warn.no_strategy.Text: Choose a strategy on the "Strategies" page or run automatic selection.
Warn.strategy_missing.Title: The selected strategy was not found
Warn.strategy_missing.Text: The strategy was removed or is not installed. Choose another one on the "Strategies" page.
Warn.generate_failed.Title: The engine settings could not be prepared
Warn.generate_failed.Text: The last start attempt failed. Open "Diagnostics" → "Configuration check" for details.
Warn.bad_config.Title: Some settings have invalid values
Warn.bad_config.Text: Some options are ignored and default values are used instead. Check "Settings".
Warn.bad_config.TextWith: These options are ignored and default values are used instead: {0}. Correct them in "Settings".
Warn.config_was_invalid.Title: The settings did not pass the check
Warn.config_was_invalid.Text: The new settings did not pass the built-in check, but the previous ones did not pass it either, so the changes were applied anyway. If sites do not open, open "Diagnostics" → "Configuration check".
Warn.list_missing.Title: An enabled list was not found
Warn.list_missing.Text: One of the enabled lists was removed or is not installed. Check the "Lists" page.
Warn.source_not_downloaded.Title: A subscription has not been downloaded yet
Warn.source_not_downloaded.Text: An enabled subscription list has never been downloaded, so it is skipped for now. Open "Lists" → "Subscriptions" and press "Update now".
Warn.profile_unfiltered.Title: A strategy profile applies to all sites
Warn.profile_unfiltered.Text: One of the profiles of the strategy has no site or network list, so it processes all traffic on its ports. This is normal for some strategies (for example, Discord voice), but if sites that should stay untouched break, choose another strategy.
Warn.wide_port_range.Title: The strategy processes a wide port range
Warn.wide_port_range.Text: The strategy sends many ports to the engine, which loads the PC more. If the connection slows down, choose another strategy.
Warn.empty_profile_removed.Title: Empty profiles were removed from the strategy
Warn.empty_profile_removed.Text: The strategy contains empty profiles (extra --new); they are ignored. Nothing needs to be done.
Warn.strategy_option_ignored.Title: Some strategy options are ignored
Warn.strategy_option_ignored.Text: Options that zaprett sets itself are ignored in the strategy text. Nothing needs to be done.
Warn.not_running.Title: The bypass is on but not running
Warn.not_running.Text: The bypass should work, but the engine process is not running: it probably stopped with an error. Press "Restart"; if it does not help, look at "Diagnostics".
Warn.test_running.Title: Strategy selection is running
Warn.test_running.Text: During the check the bypass keeps working: strategies are tried by a separate test engine.
Warn.low_memory.Title: The enabled lists are very large
Warn.low_memory.Text: The enabled services or subscriptions use large lists: the engine needs more memory. Turn off large subscriptions if the PC slows down.
Warn.monitor_degraded.Title: Sites of the enabled services stopped opening
Warn.monitor_degraded.Text: Several checks of the availability monitor in a row failed: the provider may have changed the blocking. Run automatic strategy selection. If automatic repair is on, zaprett is already looking for a working strategy.
Warn.game_filter_no_ipsets.Title: The game filter is not working: no IP network list
Warn.game_filter_no_ipsets.Text: The game filter processes only addresses from the enabled IP network lists, so that the rest of the traffic stays untouched. No such list is enabled now, so the filter is skipped. Enable the IP network list of the game on the "Lists" page, or turn the game filter off in "Settings".
Warn.dns_plain.Title: DNS requests go without encryption
Warn.dns_plain.Text: For some of the enabled services the provider may substitute DNS answers; then the site does not open even though the bypass works. Encrypted DNS hides the requests from the provider.
Warn.ipv6_wan_unhandled.Title: IPv6 connections go without the bypass
Warn.ipv6_wan_unhandled.Text: Your internet connection has IPv6, but zaprett processes only IPv4 now. Sites that open over IPv6 are not unblocked. Turn on "Process IPv6" in "Settings".
Warn.windivert_foreign.Title: Another program uses WinDivert
Warn.windivert_foreign.Text: A driver of another traffic interceptor (for example GoodbyeDPI) is running. Two interceptors interfere with each other. See "Diagnostics" → "Conflicting programs".
Warn.conflicts_found.Title: Conflicting programs found
Warn.conflicts_found.Text: Some programs on this PC can stop the bypass. See "Diagnostics" → "Conflicting programs".
Wizard.Title: Setting up zaprett
Wizard.Intro.Title: Open what your provider slows down
Wizard.Intro.Lead: zaprett changes only the first packets of connections to the chosen sites, so the equipment of the provider does not recognise them. Everything else goes as usual. Setup takes a couple of minutes.
Wizard.Intro.Does1: Opens sites that are slowed down or blocked by analysing traffic (DPI): YouTube, Discord and others.
Wizard.Intro.Does2: Works only for the chosen services; banks and government services are excluded.
Wizard.Intro.Does3: Checks by itself whether the sites open and finds a working strategy.
Wizard.Intro.DoesNot1: It is not a VPN: your address does not change, and sites that block Russia themselves stay closed.
Wizard.Intro.DoesNot2: It does not help against blocking by IP address or DNS substitution alone (encrypted DNS helps with the latter).
Wizard.Intro.DoesNot3: It does not unblock traffic of other devices shared from this PC.
Wizard.Intro.Privacy: zaprett sends nothing about you anywhere: no telemetry, no accounts.
Wizard.Services.Title: Which services do not work well?
Wizard.Services.Lead: Mark them — zaprett turns on ready-made lists of their sites. Where zaprett cannot help, it says so honestly.
Wizard.NothingSelectedText: Mark at least one service to continue.
Wizard.Conflicts.Title: Checking other programs
Wizard.Conflicts.Lead: Programs that also intercept traffic can stop the bypass. zaprett looks for them before starting.
Wizard.Conflicts.Blocking: Found a program that blocks the bypass
Wizard.Conflicts.BlockingText: Fix it as described below, otherwise the sites may not open. You can continue anyway.
Wizard.Apply.Title: Starting and checking
Wizard.Step.Lists: Turn on the lists of the chosen services
Wizard.NoTargets: The chosen services have no addresses to check.
Wizard.FixHint: Different providers block in different ways, so the default strategy may not suit yours.
Wizard.Fix.Title: Let's find what works with your provider
Wizard.Fix.Lead: First find out how the provider blocks: if it substitutes DNS or blocks addresses, another strategy will not help, and the check tells what will. Then zaprett can try strategies one by one.
Wizard.Fix.SelectText: Quick selection: about 12 strategies, a few minutes. The bypass keeps working meanwhile; the best strategy is applied by itself.
Wizard.Done.Title: Done: zaprett is set up and running
Wizard.Done.Text: The icon in the notification area shows the state. If sites stop opening later, zaprett notices it and suggests automatic strategy selection.
Wizard.Done.PartTitle: zaprett is running, but not everything opens
Wizard.Done.PartText: Some services still do not open. Look at "Diagnostics" for the reason or run the full strategy selection on the "Strategies" page.
Wizard.AutostartText: Recommended: the bypass is on right after Windows starts.
